id: title:Gilbert09:avoid unix epoch afterdate on first incremental sync

review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion pipeline stability for Fillout connector; prevents API 400 errors on initial batch, preserving data stream integrity.
review.reason: The change replaces a rejected Unix epoch timestamp with a sentinel value compatible with the Fillout API, preventing ingestion failures. Tests were added to guard against regression. This is a substantive, bounded correctness improvement.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies on supplied observations; no independent execution or runtime failure demonstration. Benefit is inferred from API compatibility rather than observed production incident avoidance.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of the test assertions or the execution of the test, so while the test existence and its expected behavior are clear, the actual runtime behavior and failure handling are not demonstrated. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: The implementation of the Fillout warehouse source was changed to use a sentinel value of '1970-01-01T00:00:01Z' instead of '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z' for the initial incremental window cursor, because the Fillout API rejects the Unix epoch with a 400 error.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents the warehouse ingestion pipeline from failing when syncing the first batch of submissions from Fillout, which could otherwise result in a 400 API error and a broken data stream.

observations.behavior: The test file was updated to import the newly exposed helper function `_fillout_incremental_window` and a new test was added to assert that the initial value is not the Unix epoch.
observations.posthog_connection: This adds a regression check to ensure the workaround is preserved and does not regress to the rejected value.
